stages.title: Requirements
stages.questionPrompt: Clarify the requirements. What's in scope and what isn't?
stages.howToAnswer: Capture the rules tightly. Decide whether to scope: AI opponent, multi-game match, network play. State assumptions out loud.

avoid: Building features not requested (AI opponent, networking)

stages.title: Entities & Relationships
stages.questionPrompt: What are the core entities and how do they relate?
stages.howToAnswer: Pick the orchestrator. Decide what owns each piece of state. Avoid an anaemic God class.

avoid: Putting all logic on a single God class

stages.sampleAnswer:
- REPLACE: orchestrates the workflow.
- REPLACE: owns the state.
- REPLACE: action / move primitive.

stages.title: Class Design
stages.questionPrompt: Define the classes — fields and methods. Keep rules with the entity that owns the state.
stages.howToAnswer: Sketch each class with explicit method signatures and what they return / throw. Use enums for fixed states.

must: Methods return useful types (not bare bool)
avoid: Returning bool from methods that need richer state

stages.sampleAnswer:
```
enum State { IN_PROGRESS, ... }

class A:
  field1: Type
  field2: Type
  method(args) -> ReturnType:
    REPLACE
```

stages.title: Implementation
stages.questionPrompt: Pseudo-code the major methods and trace through one scenario.
stages.howToAnswer: The hardest method is the meaty one — write it carefully. Then trace a concrete sequence end-to-end.

stages.title: Extensibility
stages.questionPrompt: How would the design extend for: REPLACE follow-up scenarios?
stages.howToAnswer: Stay high-level. Point at the seams in the design that make the change clean.

avoid: Rewriting the design when a simple extension suffices
